steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: translate a requirement into ownership
steps.detail: Begin with a written requirement and the relevant CRV-ARCH-HLD-002 v2.0 and CRV-FUNC-001 v1.0 sections when a real feature is proposed. The source snapshot explains what currently exists, while the approved specification states the intended business behavior; a disagreement is a decision to resolve, not an excuse to silently rewrite architecture. Identify the owner of each durable fact, the caller, the trusted actor and every cross-service boundary. Controllers receive requests, service methods enforce domain behavior, repositories persist owned facts and DTOs define allowed representations. For someone familiar with SAP, think of this as locating the authoritative business object and transaction boundary before creating another interface; the analogy helps orientation but does not imply a shared distributed database transaction.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: map blast radius before implementation
steps.detail: Create a dependency inventory with rows for schema, API, events, clients, configuration, scheduled work and external providers. For each, state unchanged, changed or unknown and why. A display-only improvement should not require new payment credentials or a seven-service deployment. A new persisted order fact may require more than a UI change because existing records, projections and documents must remain coherent. Keep pricing, commissions, delivery radius, compliance, cancellation and refund decisions in an unresolved-policy ledger until approved. Avoid importing Node backend patterns from the retired backend when the owner is a Spring Boot service. Prefer the smallest compatible extension to an existing owner over adding a service simply to organize a field.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: perform a change-impact review
steps.detail: Choose one synthetic read-only feature from the preceding courses. Write its owner, actors, input/output contract, data lineage, affected files, tests, operational permissions, rollback and explicit non-goals. Add a second contrasting example involving a financial rule and mark the approval it would need rather than implementing it. Use the actual repository tree to locate candidate files, then open those files to verify their roles. Record which assumptions come from code, approved requirements or the training brief. Deliver an impact map that explicitly says payment, delivery, infrastructure and unrelated services remain unchanged for the selected read-only exercise.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: an architecture-aligned change proposal with source paths, approved-versus-proposed behavior and a narrow blast radius. A reviewer must be able to reject scope expansion before code is written.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: use the Academy itself as a reference slice
steps.detail: Read AcademyCatalog, AcademyController and AcademyService with the web Academy route and dashboard. The catalog loads reviewed learning data; the controller derives the authenticated actor and enforces operation-specific roles; the service calculates scores, persists learner progress and awards XP; the BFF forwards only an allowed route; the dashboard renders the approved response. This is a concrete vertical slice, not a generic microservices diagram. Trace one quiz submission including the content version, course/lesson IDs, answer list and stable request receipt. Identify where the server rejects incomplete answers, stale versions and a receipt reused with different answers. The client must not choose its own score, completion timestamp or earned XP.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: transactions, replay and isolation
steps.detail: AcademyService serializes learner writes using a database row lock, persists a request fingerprint and enforces unique XP reward keys. Read AcademyPersistenceTest to see the difference between one repeated request receipt and a new attempt. The updated course-bonus test iterates all current lessons rather than assuming a course always contains two. Explain why a one-process in-memory set would not preserve these guarantees after restart. Also distinguish retained lifetime XP from version-scoped completion. A reading-only enhancement should not rename lessons or reset the assessment version merely to make a new curriculum appear. Assessment changes require an explicit migration/progress policy; extra prose and labs do not grant additional privileges or certify employee competence.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: implement one complete local feature
steps.detail: Create training/academy-read-only-summary and implement the synthetic learner-summary brief from the Auth track. Submit complete files for controller/DTO, service mapping, Java tests, constrained client route where necessary, runtime parser and UI states. Add no schema unless an approved durable fact truly needs it. Use synthetic identities and mock dependencies first; database tests require only the documented disposable database. Run the Java and web gates and attach their results. Present the implementation to a reviewer who attempts wrong-role, wrong-owner, malformed-response and duplicate-request cases. The exercise is complete only when you can explain each layer and demonstrate the negative cases, not merely display a successful screen.

lessons.lab: Capstone deliverables: full file tree and contents, requirements/contract, request trace, tests, synthetic evidence, compatibility note and rollback plan. This is a local assessed exercise; it does not deploy an unapproved feature or alter existing services.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: design evidence that can fail
steps.detail: Read .github/workflows/craves-academy-ci.yml. Its backend job starts a disposable PostgreSQL database, validates source provenance and runs Academy core and persistence tests; its web job runs focused tests, lint, typecheck and a production build. Match each command to the property it proves. Test reports must retain discovered, executed, failed and skipped counts. A class guarded by an environment variable can be skipped even when Maven exits successfully. The correct response is to run the isolated suite in its intended environment or state that it was not executed, not to relabel the skip as a pass. Keep production credentials and providers outside ordinary CI.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: avoid green tests with weak assertions
steps.detail: An assertion that an object is non-null does not prove owner isolation, amount correctness or duplicate safety. For each invariant, identify the observable failure a test must catch. Use a deliberate local mutation to demonstrate that the assertion fails when the protection is removed, then restore the code. Do not weaken a test or mark it ignored simply to achieve a green pipeline. A public source repository exposes learning answer keys; hiding keys in the initial API prevents accidental disclosure but does not make these quizzes tamper-proof examinations. Treat reading checks as formative practice and require working capstone evidence and peer review for engineering readiness.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: assemble and challenge a test matrix
steps.detail: Write at least ten acceptance cases for the chosen capstone: success, anonymous, wrong role, wrong owner, malformed input, malformed upstream response, absent old-row/old-response field, duplicate attempt where relevant, concurrent update where relevant and dependency failure. Assign unit, integration, contract or manual acceptance evidence to each. Run the actual selected suites and include their exact revision. Deliberately break one guard only in the local training branch and show the intended test fails; restore it before submission. Record unexecuted browser/device, load and production checks separately. No destructive tests may target a real database, and no provider call may be used to make a mocked test look end to end.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: a test matrix with meaningful assertions, a controlled failing-then-passing demonstration and honest skipped/not-run entries. The reviewer must reject a green build that cannot detect the capstone's main security or consistency risk.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: preserve an existing service during a narrow release
steps.detail: For Academy, the runtime owner is Auth. Inspect azure-pipelines-auth-service.yml and scripts/release/deploy-single-service-preserve-runtime.sh in a full repository clone. The existing pipeline builds the Auth image and uses a helper that captures and compares runtime configuration while checking readiness and retaining a previous-image rollback path. It is a narrower deployment boundary than azure-pipelines-backend-completion.yml. Preserve the existing service connection, secret references, feature flags, ingress, managed identity, revision mode and one-replica scale configuration. A single-replica setting is not a promise that a deployment never briefly has an old and new revision present during readiness checks. No new paid resource is required for a curriculum expansion.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: authentication failures are not infrastructure permission
steps.detail: An Azure OIDC login depends on an exact trusted subject, issuer and audience. A repository branch subject and an environment subject are different identities; the presence of client/tenant/subscription settings does not prove the selected workflow subject is trusted. Inspect the existing approved workflow and error before changing anything. A read-only preflight that fails to log in has not verified or changed the deployment. Do not bypass approvals, expand IAM or rotate working credentials as a convenience. Record source publication, CI completion, image build, deployment and authenticated Academy acceptance as separate milestones. Unobserved steps remain pending even if earlier steps passed.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: prepare an operator-ready release packet
steps.detail: For the synthetic capstone, record reviewed source SHA, CI run IDs, artifact digest, exact target service, previous healthy revision, configuration fingerprints, migration compatibility, route and smoke cases. Include an Auth-only deployment instruction and explicitly prohibit unrelated service release. Before any real operator run, current backup/PITR and runtime evidence must be verified; a copied old timestamp is not current evidence. Prepare checks for authorized catalog read, source viewing, quiz retry with no duplicate XP, denied customer access and another learner remaining unchanged. Leave live fields blank/pending until observed. The lab itself is a rehearsal and must not update Azure, provision resources, change secrets or issue OTPs.

lessons.lab: Completion evidence: a release packet another engineer can execute and audit without reconstructing intent from chat. It must identify the exact narrow deployment and distinguish what was tested locally, in CI and in production.

steps.label: Enterprise walkthrough: investigate from evidence, not labels
steps.detail: Start an incident record with expected behavior, actual behavior, timestamp, exact route/action, installed/deployed version and sanitized correlation/resource IDs. Follow the failing boundary through client, BFF, gateway, Java, owned persistence, broker and provider as appropriate. The first missing or contradictory checkpoint is more useful than a broad statement that the platform is down. Distinguish a dashboard filter hiding history from data deletion, a provider-create timeout from no booking, and an old client parser from an unavailable backend. Preserve audit trails and transaction records. Recovery should be the smallest reversible action supported by the evidence, with a regression test and runbook correction after containment.

steps.label: Enterprise failure analysis: capacity and permissions remain separate decisions
steps.detail: An error may be a logic defect, bad contract, missing configuration, dependency outage or exhausted capacity. Measure before scaling. Record request mix, concurrency, duration, data volume, error rate and high-percentile latency when designing a nonproduction load test. Current one-replica deployment and unit-test success do not establish one-million-user capacity. Do not promise no future errors. Bound retries, connection pools, queues and timeouts according to inspected implementation and approved operating limits. Training records and a Bayesian practice signal are not validated measures of employee aptitude; they must not be used for employment decisions or to grant production permissions automatically.

steps.label: Enterprise lab: pass an operational defense review
steps.detail: Present the capstone and respond to four tabletop incidents: wrong-owner access, malformed upstream response, uncertain external action and unhealthy newly deployed revision. For each, give the safe next read, immediate containment, forbidden destructive action, compatibility check, rollback/reconciliation and regression test. Submit an evidence ledger and unresolved-work list with owners. A reviewer assesses contract/ownership, implementation completeness, negative tests, retry/recovery, privacy and release discipline as separate criteria. Any leaked secret, unauthorized production write, invented business policy or destroyed transaction evidence is a rejection regardless of quiz score. Complete missing evidence in an isolated lab rather than improvising against production.

lessons.lab: Final assessment: the learner demonstrates one working local end-to-end feature and defends its security, data lineage, tests, client behavior and rollback. Reading completion and XP are learning aids, not a certification, employment ranking or automatic production access grant.
